name: Leonidas Guibas
title: Paul Pigott Professor of Engineering and Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
research_topics: 3D generative modeling and controllable shape/asset generation

current_direction: Controllable and part-aware 3D asset generation, including training-free test-time spatial control
Flow-matching generative models and few-step imitation distillation for fast sampling
Direct mesh generation with equivariant, structure-aware architectures
Gaussian-splatting scene representations: continual updates, distractor removal, decomposition into primitives
Latent multimodal reasoning for spatial understanding in vision-language models
current_direction_basis: Inferred only from 2025-2026 items collected in this task via OpenAlex (author A5065368881, 26 works dated 2025-01-01 or later) plus arXiv abstract pages. Specifically: SpaceControl (arXiv 2512.05343, Dec 2025) for training-free test-time spatial control of 3D generation; PASTA (3DV 2026) for part-aware controllable shape generation; pi-Flow (arXiv 2510.14974, ICLR 2026) and Gaussian Mixture Flow Matching Models (arXiv 2504.05304) for flow-matching / few-step distillation; MeshFlow (2026, DOI 10.1145/3799902.3811195) for equivariant flow-matching mesh generation; SuperDec (ICCV 2025), CL-Splats (ICCV 2025), Self-Calibrating Gaussian Splatting (ICCV 2025), SplatTalk (ICCV 2025) and SpotLessSplats (ACM TOG, Mar 2025) for the Gaussian-splatting cluster; Mull-Tokens (arXiv 2512.10941, CVPR 2026 Findings) and Perspective-Aware Reasoning in Vision-Language Models (ICCV 2025) for multimodal latent spatial reasoning. NOT based on the biography text on the Stanford pages, which still emphasizes sensor networks, GPS traces and macromolecule modeling, nor on the lab's own publication list, which stops at 2024.

evidence.title: MeshFlow: Mesh Generation with Equivariant Flow Matching
evidence.summary: Generates 3D meshes directly with an equivariant flow-matching model, addressing the permutation invariance of mesh vertices and faces. Guibas is a co-author with Qi Sun, Kiyohiro Nakayama, Qixing Huang, Gordon Wetzstein and others. Publication date 2026-07-16 per OpenAlex; venue reported by Semantic Scholar as International Conference on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques (SIGGRAPH family).
evidence.venue: International Conference on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques

evidence.title: Mull-Tokens: Modality-Agnostic Latent Thinking
evidence.summary: Introduces modality-agnostic latent tokens that let a multimodal model hold intermediate reasoning state in either image or text form, improving four spatial-reasoning benchmarks by ~3% on average and up to +16% on a puzzle-solving split. arXiv comment on the fetched abstract page states 'Accepted to CVPR 2026 (Findings Track)'. arXiv posting date 2025-12-11.
evidence.venue: arXiv preprint; accepted to CVPR 2026 (Findings Track) per arXiv comment

evidence.title: pi-Flow: Policy-Based Few-Step Generation via Imitation Distillation
evidence.summary: Modifies the output layer of a student flow model to predict a network-free policy, producing dynamic flow velocities at future substeps for fast ODE integration; reports 1-NFE FID of 2.85 on ImageNet 256^2. Lead author Hansheng Chen is a current Guibas Lab graduate student. arXiv comment on the fetched abstract page states 'ICLR 2026'. arXiv posting date 2025-10-16.
evidence.venue: arXiv preprint; ICLR 2026 per arXiv comment

evidence.title: SpaceControl: Introducing Test-Time Spatial Control to 3D Generative Modeling
evidence.summary: A training-free test-time method for explicit spatial control of 3D asset generation that accepts geometric inputs from coarse primitives to detailed meshes, with a control parameter trading geometric fidelity against realism, plus an interactive real-time superquadric editing interface. Co-authored with Guibas Lab postdoc Francis Engelmann and graduate student Ian Huang. Posted 2025-12-05.

evidence.title: SuperDec: 3D Scene Decomposition with Superquadric Primitives
evidence.summary: Creates compact yet expressive 3D scene representations by decomposing scenes into superquadric primitives, rather than using primitives purely for photorealistic reconstruction. Published at ICCV 2025 (OpenAlex publication date 2025-10-19).
evidence.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV) 2025

state_rationale: No formal opening was found. The lab site has no join/openings/prospective-students page and contains zero occurrences of undergraduate-facing language, and it lists no undergraduate members — so OPENING is not justified. But the group is clearly and heavily active: OpenAlex reports 26 works with a publication date of 2025-01-01 or later under author A5065368881, including two dated 2026 (most recent 2026-07-16), with 2026 acceptances at CVPR 2026 Findings (Mull-Tokens), ICLR 2026 (pi-Flow) and 3DV 2026 (PASTA), and a full roster of three postdocs and eleven graduate students who could mentor a student. Guibas also teaches CS 233 / CME 251 in Spring 2025-26, giving a natural point of contact, and a direct email is published on the lab site. That combination makes a well-targeted cold email from a Stanford undergraduate reasonable, so OUTREACH rather than WATCH. Note for the student: the lab's own publication list is stale (newest entry seen is 2024), so any outreach should reference the 2025-2026 arXiv/conference work rather than the site's listings, and should probably be addressed toward a specific postdoc or graduate student's project.
